newsitem.title: USA: SKI JUMPING-FINN TO HEAD U.S. EFFORT.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-FINN TO HEAD U.S. EFFORT.

text.p: Former Finnish ski jumping head coach Kari Ylianttila Monday was appointed head coach of the struggling U.S. ski jumping team.
Ylianttila, whose athletes earned 14 medals in the Olympics or World Championships between 1987 and 1994, replaces Zane Palmer, who will take over as jumping coach for the U.S. nordic combined team.
A 1980 Olympic jumper, Ylianttila spent 12 years on Finland's national coaching staff before resigning after the 1994 Lillehammer Games.

Ylianttila takes over a team that has struggled so badly in recent years that no American jumpers were sent to the World Championships in Norway in February due to their lack of ability to compete on a world class level.
With Ylianttila as head coach, Finns won all three gold medals at the 1998 Olympics in Calgary and collected four medals, including a pair of golds, at the 1989 World Championships in Lahti, Finland.
